brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

requirements.requirement: Shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books
requirements.evidence: Built 2-storey 4-cell base (piece:0,0,0;full + 3 neighbors on level 0, 4 cells on level 1) with open levels usable as shelves; configurator checks fit/collision only (meshClash clear) and does not verify materials, strength or load ratings. Parts are 3D-printed in user-chosen material, so no 50 kg rating can be claimed - see bom notes.

Two notch drawer frames installed: notch:0#-1,1#notch0 (hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf) and notch:0#0,2#notch1 (hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm) with support bases piece:-1,2,0;half-s and piece:1,2,0;half-s creating drawer bays; drawer inserts (addDrawer sockets s202/s203) are offered but not yet placed, so drawers are provisioned not completed.

finish.summary: Built a 2-level hex shelf frame (4+4 cells) with two drawer-frame bays ready for drawer inserts. Cannot meet 50 kg load rating as configurator verifies fit only and parts are 3D-printed plastic; drawer bays are in place but drawer inserts not yet fitted.

M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
